attempts.note: Vendor OpenAPI 3.0.4 behind the public Swashbuckle UI at https://apim.puntosolidario.gob.do/swagger/index.html (its index.js lists the single document '/swagger/v2/swagger.json'). 643 paths / 935 operations / 287 schemas. Host found in the Punto Solidario web client bundle (https://psweb.puntosolidario.gob.do/js/app.*.js), which calls https://apim.puntosolidario.gob.do/api/authentication/request, the same login route the adaptor uses.
psweb is a Vue SPA that answers every path with index.html; no spec there.

Adaptor request issue: API docs were shared privately ('Ask me for API docs'); the only sample is get('/casos', {query:{id}}), which has no matching route in the vendor spec (cases live under /api/CasoInfo and /api/External/adess/consulta/casos).
No vendor GitHub org or SDK; code search finds only the OpenFn adaptor and domain lists.

notes: Punto Solidario (Dominican Republic social-programmes single window, ADESS/Superate) runs an ASP.NET Core Web API at https://apim.puntosolidario.gob.do whose Swashbuckle UI is public; its 'Punto Solidario v2' OpenAPI 3.0.4 document is committed verbatim as upstream.json and served unchanged apart from info.x-openfn-adaptor. It replaces the July 2026 stub, which invented /beneficiarios, /subsidios and /transacciones paths that do not exist; the real API has 935 operations over 104 controllers (CasoInfo, Ciudadano, Hogar, Miembro, TramiteBeneficiario, Transaccion, Tarjeta, Nomina, External ADESS/SIUBEN/SENASA proxies, OData query routes, CSV/PDF exports). The adaptor authenticates with POST {baseUrl}/authentication/request {username,password} and sends the returned token as a Bearer header; that is the spec's POST /api/Authentication/request (TokenRequest), so configuration.baseUrl should be https://apim.puntosolidario.gob.do/api (ASP.NET routing is case-insensitive). Vendor gaps kept as-is: the document declares no servers and no securitySchemes, and 914 of 935 operations declare a bare 200 'OK' with no response body schema, so data-schemas/ holds only the handful of DTOs the vendor typed. Whether OpenFn's 'TEST API' credential points at this host or a separate test deployment is not public; the adaptor surface (generic http.get/post/request) is fully covered either way.
